imagem-docker.d: Ordered stack of filesystem layers + a config (environment, entrypoint, labels, rootfs.diff_ids) + a manifest that lists everything by SHA-256. It's the “frozen operating system” vLLM runs in.

camada-imagem.d: A tar with the file differences produced by one Dockerfile instruction (RUN, COPY). Identified by the SHA-256 of its content (DiffID). LABEL, ENV and ARG don't create a file layer.

tag-imagem.d: Mutable name in the registry (:0.1.1, :latest) that points to a manifest. It can be republished pointing at a different image, like a git branch.

digest-imagem.d: The @sha256:… identifier of an image's manifest. Because it's the hash of the content, it's immutable: pinning the image by digest guarantees the same bytes on any node, on any day.

indice-multiarch.d: A manifest of manifests: one name points to per-platform variants (linux/arm64, linux/amd64). When shipping via docker save | docker load, pass --platform, or the load may break.

image-key.d: Image identity the GLM launcher uses to compare head and worker: a short hash of RootFS.Layers (the DiffIDs). Unlike .Id and the RepoDigests, it survives overlay2 vs. containerd and docker save | load.

cache-de-build.d: Docker reuses a layer as long as the instruction, the copied files and every layer below it are unchanged. Changing layer \(k\) rebuilds everything from \(k\) upward; that's why whatever rarely changes goes at the bottom.

recipe-stamp.d: SHA-256 of the sorted list of hashes of the files GLM's Dockerfile copies, stored as LABEL glm53.recipe.stamp. If the repository diverges from the label, the launcher rebuilds the image (unless SKIP_BUILD=1).

extensao-nativa.d: Compiled library (.so, C++/CUDA) that Python imports, like exllamav3_ext. It must be compiled for the host CPU (aarch64 on the GB10) and for the GPU (list of CUDA architectures).

stub.d: Minimal stand-in implementation that keeps the interface and turns the functionality off. An honest stub answers “not supported” where it's asked and aborts (std::abort()) if anyone uses the disabled path. A silent stub (no-op) is only safe behind a gate that keeps anyone from reaching it.

bind-mount.d: Mounting a host file or directory inside the container (-v host:container[:ro]). The mounted file covers the image's file at that path; mounts are fixed when the container is created.

camada-gravavel.d: Copy-on-write layer on top of the image, holding the writes made inside the container (such as hotfixes applied at boot). It survives docker restart and only goes away when the container is recreated.

recriar-container.d: Removing it and creating it again (./stop + ./start, compose down/up): clean writable layer, mounts and environment read again. Different from docker restart, which restarts the same container with its creation-time configuration.

source-exact.d: A patch that only applies to exactly known bytes: it pins the SHA-256 (and size) of the stock file and of the result, builds and compiles the post-image in memory, publishes atomically and re-verifies itself. An unknown source becomes a refusal.

idempotencia.d: Applying twice has the same effect as applying once: \(P(P(x)) = P(x)\). An idempotent patch recognizes its own result (the patched pin or a marker) and exits successfully without writing.

publicacao-atomica.d: Write to a temporary file in the same directory, fsync it and swap it for the target with os.replace (POSIX rename). Readers see either the whole old file or the whole new one, never half, even if the process dies midway.

patch-por-ancora.d: An edit that looks for an exact snippet of the original file (the anchor must occur exactly once), validates the result (ast.parse/compile) and aborts without writing if anything doesn't match. It tolerates changes in other parts of the file.

composicao-de-patches.d: The final file is \(P_n \circ \cdots \circ P_1(\text{stock})\). Two patches commute if neither rewrites what the other reads (anchor) or writes (region); when one rewrites the other's region or anchor, the order (e.g., GLM53_OVERLAY_ORDER) becomes part of the recipe.

paridade-de-ranks.d: Every rank in a tensor-parallel group must run the same bytes (image, patches, order) and the same knobs. Different code can launch different collectives, and NCCL hangs waiting.

precedencia-de-config.d: The rule that decides which source wins when defaults, .env, environment, wrapper and CLI disagree: the first source, in priority order, that defines the key is the one that counts (equivalently, in the order the launcher applies the sources, the last one wins; in Qwen's start.sh the .env beats the command line, except for ABLIT and HF_TOKEN). Each launcher picks (and should document) its own order.

env-sourced.d: The launcher executes .env as shell code (source .env; in GLM and DeepSeek between set -a/set +a, which exports everything; in Qwen, without set -a, the variables stay only in the launcher's shell). That's why quotes vanish, \r and BOM corrupt values, and numbers go through bash arithmetic (octal, 64 bits).

crlf.d: Windows line ending (\r\n, bytes 0D 0A). In a .env read by bash, the \r sticks to the value ($'fp8\r'), invisible in the log.

bom.d: The bytes EF BB BF (U+FEFF) that some editors write at the start of UTF-8 files. At the start of a .env, the first line stops being a valid assignment for bash.

interpolacao-compose.d: Docker Compose substitutes ${VAR:-default} on the host when it reads the file; a reference with a doubled dollar sign reaches the container as $VAR and is only evaluated by the container's shell, at runtime. Two phases, two environments.

launcher.d: Script that orchestrates the recipe on both nodes (e.g., start.sh): configuration, preflight, image, weights, sync, worker → head, wait with a deadline, warmup and canary, with defined exit codes and logs from both nodes in a known place.

restart-policy.d: Docker rule for restarting a container that exited (no, unless-stopped…). In multi-node tensor parallel it's delicate: a rank restarted on its own doesn't re-form the group with its partner.

contrato-de-saida.d: Documented meaning of each exit code of a launcher, so supervisors (systemd) act correctly. In DeepSeek: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 invalid config, 3 already running (SuccessExitStatus=3). In GLM's canary, 3 means a degenerate engine.

fixture-upstream.d: Frozen copy of an exact file from the pinned image (e.g., *-487ecf187.py.txt), used by CPU tests to prove that a patch transforms exactly that text, with no GPU and no container.

ci-em-cpu.d: Continuous integration without a GPU: script syntax, patch compilation, tests against fixtures and regression guards on every push. It proves the patch is correct; performance still requires the real hardware.

changelog.d: Versioned record of changes (Keep a Changelog format: Added/Changed/Fixed), with the issue, the measured number and the operational instruction (“recreate the containers”). It also documents what was removed and why.

backport.d: Bringing a fix from a newer upstream version into the recipe's pinned version. As a Python patch, it only works if the change doesn't require recompiling native ops or swapping the image's dependencies.

ssh-batchmode.d: ssh -o BatchMode=yes: SSH never opens an interactive prompt (password, host confirmation); if the key doesn't authenticate, it fails immediately. That's what lets a launcher drive the remote node without hanging while it waits for someone to type.

fail-fast.d: Aborting as soon as a prerequisite dies or is invalid, instead of waiting out the whole timeout: validating the configuration before stopping the healthy pair, or giving up the /health wait when the worker container has already crashed.

diff-unificado.d: The patch format of diff -u and git diff: each hunk carries context lines, removed lines (-) and added lines (+). GNU patch looks for the context and the removed lines in the file, tolerates an offset and, by default, up to 2 mismatched context lines at each end (fuzz). -p0 uses the diff's paths as they are; --forward refuses hunks that look already applied.

tag-por-hash.t: Tag from the hash of the inputs
tag-por-hash.d: An image name derived from the hash of what defines it. In the TensorFold version of the GLM recipe, the tag is v0.6.0-<h>, with \(h\) = the first 12 digits of the SHA-256 of the patches plus the pip extras, also written into the tf.patches label. Changing a patch changes the tag; the release still pins the digest of the published image, because the hash covers the inputs, not the resulting bytes.

conferencia-de-configuracoes.d: At startup, each rank packs into a list of integers the settings that change the sequence of calls; an all-gather swaps the lists, and the engine refuses to start if they differ, printing both. It turns a collective hang into an explicit error (TensorFold's GLM engine).

env-lido.d: A launcher that reads the .env line by line with a KEY=value pattern instead of source-ing it: nothing runs, quotes and comments follow their own rules, and lines outside the pattern (such as the first one, if it has a BOM) are ignored. It's what the config.sh of the TensorFold version of the GLM recipe does.
